Small-cap indexes have been rising in recent years, and many outlooks for 2018 are rosy. Yet indexes aside, greater opportunities this year may await investors who can identify promising small companies laboring in relative obscurity. Top Gold Stocks To Own For 2018
Randgold Resources (GOLD, LSE:RRS) is an LSE/NASDAQ-listed gold producer. The company’s corporate strategy is to grow by developing its production and expanding its exploration footprint across Africa. Randgold has four operating mines in Mali (Loulo, Gounkoto and Morila), one in Ivory Coast (Tongon) and one in the DRC (Kibali). It also has one advanced key developments project: Massawa in Senegal. The company has a large portfolio of exploration properties across West and Central Africa.
For many years, Randgold Resources has been the go-to name in the London gold space. Despite challenging geopolitical exposure, the high-quality, low-cost, long-life assets and now growing cash balance have provided the company with many defensive characteristics. I think Randgold is at an interesting point for equity investors. Kibali is in the process of ramping up, and the operational challenges at Tongon appear to have been settled. Although other balance sheets in the industry have improved over the past 12 months, Randgold still rates highly as a defensive exposure in the gold space. Media headlines about First Savings Financial Group (NASDAQ: FSFG ) have trended somewhat negative this week, according to Accern Sentiment. The research firm identifies negative and positive press coverage by analyzing more than 20 million news and blog sources. Accern ranks coverage of companies on a scale of negative one to one, with scores closest to one being the most favorable. First Savings Financial Group earned a media sentiment score of -0.15 on Accern’s scale. Accern also assigned news stories about the bank an impact score of 49.1494069754243 out of 100, meaning that recent press coverage is somewhat unlikely to have an effect on the company’s share price in the immediate future. The price of Bitcoin surged more than 17% to top $8,000 in a rapid move that surprised many investors this morning. The sudden rally appears to be the result of a short squeeze, according to CNBC contributor Brian Kelly. This means that investors who had been betting on a decline in the price of the world’s largest cryptocurrency had been forced to jump back and buy the currency again. A lot of people have been betting on a decline in the price of Bitcoin heading toward the April 17 tax deadline. The expectation is that many people will need to sell their Bitcoin in order to raise cash to meet tax obligations. Here’s our latest daily insight on why the Bitcoin bear market may end very soon. On Wednesday, minutes from the Fed’s most recent meeting indicated that policy makers are prepared to raise interest rates several more times in the coming months in order to stave off concerns about inflation.
